verdict.tagline: A dark puppet adventure with tight combat and linear streets.
for_you_if: you enjoy demanding soulslike combat mechanics
you want deep weapon assembly options
not_for_you_if: you prefer open exploration and branching paths
you struggle with strict parry timing windows
you need stable frame rates on release hardware

cohorts.summary: Players report mixed performance alongside linear design, weapon customization, and strict parry-focused combat.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from framerate drops and instability in specific areas such as the factory section, alongside reports of game crashes.

citations.review_text: Suprised at all the positive reviews of this game, I wish I had known that after about 3 hours of gameplay the framerate drops in the factory section to almost unplayable. The game ran at a solid 120fps until then, I feel gypped.

the game keep crashing and unstable i got very strong setup and i had no issues with it with all of the games i played but unfortunately this game crashed many times with me. i got black screen and DRAM issue while the CPU temp on 58 and GPU temp on 52 i had stuttering issues with this game while the frames says its 300fps. so i played this game once with old pc but i did refund cuz i had many problem with it now got better one but still..... i'm just disappointed cuz this game have been released for long time and still suffers from such problems

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs smoothly and performs well on PC hardware, including older setups, Steam Deck alternatives, and Linux via Proton.

citations.review_text: Really enjoying this so far. Feels like a blend of Bloodborne and Sekiro, right up my alley. And I'm happy about the performance. Runs incredibly on my older PC.
What an incredibly polished PC port!!! It runs on high settings at 100fps on my Tesla P40 on linux.

Had to buy it on PC to enjoy it for a fourth time - runs flawlessly on Linux (Fedora with Proton GE 11 - latest).

When you pay attention to the lore, and story, it's incredibly emotional. Highly recommend getting the DLC as well, it's even more emotional, The soundtrack, specifically the gramophone version of Fascination is one of my favourite takes on a classic, props to whoever thought of that. The aesthetics are unmatched, and it surprisingly looks BEAUTIFUL and runs amazing, which is not something I can say for most Unreal titles. 

It's definitely one of my favourite games of all time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the level design as very linear with cramped streets and rooftops, offering limited exploration options and blocked-off buildings.

citations.review_text: Tentative review after 4.7h of gameplay. Clearly I seek different things from my Souls-likes than general public if this is considered one of the best there is. This is mediocre at best. Very, very linear level structure with almost no options to explore. Level design is also very boring to fight in, as it's mostly cramped streets and roof tops, with not much interesting options to use while fighting. Assembling your weapons might be interesting in a long run, but for now options have been very limited. And combat itself.. something feels off, and I can't quite explain why. I like the more slower combat pace, but I don't know how else to put it, but the inputs feel a bit sluggish for a lack of better word. With a little less than 5h I should be hooked, but I don't know if I continue or not as there are much better options (at least for me) to choose from.

Summary: A by-the-numbers soulslike that elevates all traditional areas of the genre, but in so doing also magnifies its own flaws.
Combat: Combat is methodical; faster than Dark Souls 1 but slower than Dark Souls 3, AI Limit, or Stellar Blade. Movement and weapon ranges can feel stubby, dodging is mostly never the best option over parry, and charge attacks are heavily emphasized after multiple perfect parries to stagger. I found this game challenging and had to turn the difficulty down (it was nice that the game had this option). If the perfect parry system works for you, you'll like the game; it did not click for me. The weapon system is interesting in how blade + handle combinations create the weapon variety, I liked it after understanding how it worked.
Music: The music is okay, I did not find it particularly memorable. There are some areas where loudspeakers blare music for diagetic narrative reasons, I found this distracting.
Level Design: The levels are interesting, but do not leave a lasting impression. They never overstay their welcome; textures and feel are varied, and the game uses both horizontal sprawl and verticality well. Maybe it's that in a city (made up of buildings), so few of the houses could be entered, and the roads were blocked off by debris or burning objects so often that what should have been an interconnected web of sidestreets and enterable buildings was instead just a line with occasional branching paths. The both sides of unlockable shortcut doors (the blocked side and the unlockable side) looked similar from afar, I wish this was more visually distinguished.
 Lore: The game has two separate mysteries to solve in the city: murderous puppets and a petrification disease. This story was good, and the mysteries never dropped too far into predictable territory (unlike Stellar Blade or AI Limit). However, it was an odd choice to use creatures of fable. I use that term intentionally since I think this was 100% an intended choice by the dev…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features a weapon assembly system that allows players to combine different blades and handles for customization and weapon variety.

citations.review_text:
It's a good game for the most part. The combat is where it falls apart.
Where to begin? The combat doesn't match up to the enemies. Endless attacks, and if you miss 1 perfect parry you take 4-5 hits. Many weapons you find are slow to wind up a single hit and you just can't use them for some boss fights.

No animation cancelling. Accidentally had the wrong thing on your hotbar? You have to sit there for almost 3 full seconds while he does an animation, only to get hit over and over again, which doesn't take you out of said animation either.
Enemy attacks track you so well that you shouldn't bother dodging. You can wait to almost the very end of the attack to dodge or roll but even as their weapon is coming down on you, they'll rotate to follow. 

It almost feels like one team designed the systems for the player and another team designed the system for the enemies and bosses, then they tried to get them to work together and failed.

And what is with the roll? It's like, 3 feet? It is literally useless.


They give you the ability to mix and match weapons and handles, very cool, wish elden ring had something like that.
But then limit the items to modify the handles to match your build. Finite amount in game. Why? Why offer this cool experimentation feature, then punish the player for using a handle that's arcane when they're a strength build? Oh well wait til the next playthrough or hopefully farm them in end game.

This game could have been incredible with more enemy variety and better combat, needed another 6 months to a year to keep working on it.
As it is, it's maybe a 6/10 during the best parts. The organic boss designs have been really cool though, the puppet ones are all to similar.
I wish there was more variety in the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game includes an HP regain mechanic where attacking enemies after taking damage restores health.

citations.review_text:
I honestly cannot recommend this game enough. Lies Of P has to be one of the most beginner friendly soulslikes I've ever played while also keeping some sense of challenge such as it does later in the game or when you enter the dlc.

I wanna start by praising the hp regain on attacking mechanic, I feel like having something like that where I can fall back on where I can attack to regen makes me feel more comfortable trying to parry or block attacks more often than I do in other soulslikes. I know bloodborne did this system first but I really like the execution of it in this game.

Also, on the outside it may seem intimidating but overall I actually think this is a very beginner friendly soulslike, in the menu when you make a new game they offer you difficulty settings to pick from too. And still even with all that, if you go back to the hp regen mechanic I mentioned before you're gonna feel way more comfortable attempting parries or blocks rather than panic dodging.

While I wouldn't say its perfect, its a solid 9.5/10 and I highly recommend it to new soulslike players and others who have a history with the genre.

I really tried to like this game especially because I kept hearing what a masterpiece it is but after 9 hours I really can't force myself to play it anymore. I just don't vibe with the combat.

The combat seems like a mix between regular Souls gameplay and Sekiro, but it doesn't really acomplish anything. The best thing about Souls combat, rolling, is basically not present so your main tool becomes blocking and parrying which is nowhere near as smooth and thought out like in Sekiro. Parry timings are stricter and there's no rhythm to the game, a lot of enemies and bosses have these "slingshot" attacks which are just annoying as hell. Blocking is fine but with each block you lose some HP that you can get back for hitting the enemy, but, at least with a strength build, you can only hit the enemy back once before they attack again, but one hit won't refill your HP back, which means your HP is going to slowly go down and I just didn't like that. 

The game isn't all bad though, I really like the optimization. I don't have any sort of high-end PC and the game still ran at stable 144 FPS on high settings, that's great. The level design is really linear, but I'm a fan of linear games, so I liked how the areas played out. At the end of an area you often unlock a shortcut leading back to the start so you feel like you've really finished the area. I didn't really care much for the story, robots going rogue isn't super original, but I'm sure there's a lot of detail and depth if you're willing to look into it.

So yeah, my main complaint is the unsatisfying combat, it was cool apart from that. I didn't vibe with it, but clearly a lot of people do, so I won't discourage from trying it.

I on the other hand prefer skillbased games that are challenging AND intuitive.
This game has a knowlege based difficulty with attacks that artificially speed up and slow down to disrupt your block timer, and this game is built around a perfect block mechanic, if you block correctly for  0,13 seconds you beat the boss and if you dont you die, no other passive defense stat matters.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players encounter linear environments and demanding parry timing alongside built-in difficulty settings.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the level design is extremely linear and straightforward, featuring narrow streets or hallways with very little exploration or branching paths.

citations.review_text:
Fast-paced but accessible Souls-Like, and arguably the highest-quality entry in the genre to-date outside of FromSoftware's catalog (with only maybe the in-development 'Mortal Shell II' as the closest point of comparison, based off its demo), which cements an identity of its own beyond its immediate, blatant, influences via highly-tuned combat mechanics beyond a stamina-bar and dodge-roll, in addition the unique, visually distinct, setting replete with the accoutrements of late 1800's Europe, great voice acting, and immaculate soundtrack. There's a lot the game does well, and exceptionally so, in its gameplay and presentation, very much deserving its 'Very Positive' steam review score; but while superbly-polished, and nailing a very specific aesthetic for its world, has very apparent, pronounced, flaws that keep me from adoring it to the same extent as most other Steam reviews gushing over it. 

Aside from the concessions of the Unreal Engine the game is built in, level-design is exceedingly linear, and without branching, to an extent I have not seen in other Souls-likes, or the Souls series itself ('Dark Souls III', the most linear in the series, feeling immensely more broad and open in comparison), much of the game feeling like following streets or hallways (that are very well decorated, and rarely look identical to one another) between the different zones, with the meager amount of exploration available almost always rewarding you with only a small variety of consumables or upgrade materials you can, eventually, buy from merchants anyway. Likewise, while a considerably more narratively-driven experience, with excellent voice work, the English translation/localization in dialogue and item descriptions is commonly phrased awkwardly, making parsing the exact function of more niche upgrades or abilities less-than intuitive. One such consumable item reads to 'temporarily restore HP', and instead restores HP over time; the status conditions 'Shock' and 'Electric Shock'…

Honesty when i first played this game i found it like a very good game but couldn't really compare to Soulsborne games only because of exploration, i thought it was too straightforward, now replaying it after the drop of the dlc i'm loving it and i deem it equal or superior to some soulsborne games, so if you are a fan of the genre it's a must play, also get the dlc (i paid for it, i recieved as a gift only the base game), the dlc seems good AF

Good art style. Good music. Good combat.  Pretty linear, but it benefits from it. Story is easy to follow. Creepy. In chapter 11 the devs just go "screw it, this isn't a soulslike, it's just dark souls straight up"

8.5/10

Great Soulslike (bloodborne meets sekiro) with its own spin of it, beautiful Environment, insane Weapon variety mechanic with being able to change the handles (moveset) of a blade (damage). Some good bosses, more somewhat poorly designed ones. Combat is fun, Story (Spin of Pinocchios adventures) is really enjoyable too.

Imo missing some exploration in those beautiful Environments. Every chapter is on the shorter side aside from the last one.

Also the longer I played the more the fps dropped, there are some fixes online.

Overall 8/10 as mentioned before, some boss designs are definitely questionable, not much exploration which I hope will be expanded on a sequel.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that dialogue and companion commentary can feel overly explicit and transparent, detracting from the atmospheric tension.

citations.review_text:
Very good game. I like the aesthetic, the gameplay feels very smooth (I don't like how enemies recover some damage recently dealt, but I understand the idea), the atmosphere is great, there's entrancing music. It's a bit easy for my tastes, but that's neither here nor there. I have one major gripe though I need to get off my chest.

While the story is fine, sometimes very good, the dialogue writing is very blatant and obvious. Without exception, characters either act extremely cartoonish, express their character traits to you, or explain the narrative playing out before you. "Puppets killed my sister! Die, you puppet!" "Well, I'm sure I don't need to introduce myself. You've never hear of me, really?!" "Gee, that painting is behaving really strangely. It reminds me of the painter who painted it who told me souls can live within paintings." I like the opaque, mysterious storytelling of FromSoftware, and comparing that to this really highlights how much more rewarding storytelling is when the player is actively involved in interpreting the story and coming to their own understanding and conclusions about it.

The worst culprit is Gemini, a luminescent cricket who lives inside a lantern you take with you. He chimes in constantly with obvious thoughts about everything. It completely undercuts the atmosphere. You come across a deserted town with corpses and blood and violent puppets everywhere, and instead of letting the horror of the situation sink in, Gemini goes "Geez, this is awful. Did puppets do this?" I wonder, Gemini.

This game is legitimately a masterpiece, even if you don't like souls-likes please play through this game for the story and characters it's absolutely phenomenal, especially the DLC. 

Although please do not make the same mistake I did, I beg of anyone that has yet to play this game please go on NexusMods and download the mod that COMPLETELY removes Gemini AND his subtitles, he adds absolutely NOTHING of any value to the game and actively DETRACTS from some incredibly strong moments especially in the DLC, he is unfunny garbage tier meaningless dialogue in what is otherwise a phenomenally written game. 

I'm truly not joking, it's a simple drag and drop file, it's incredibly easy to do before even booting up the game and I promise you your experience will be VASTLY superior. Trust me this game deserves to have it's mood intact for many of the moments this pointless addition of a "character" completely and utterly ruins.

claims.claim: Reviewers find the parry timing difficult to learn, noting that players must block unusually early before enemy attacks land.

citations.review_text: I like the story and atmosphere, but what this game is at the end of the day is a souls-like with a bad dodge and an even worse parry, the two fundamental combat elements of the genre.  A lot of the game is very frustrating because you are fighting with the exceptionally bad parry timing.  You have to block really early in the animation so if the attack has already started, you are too late.  It is poor design and extremely frustrating in what could be a great game otherwise.

My first souls game that I had a hard time playing. The atmosphere, soundtrack and the overall visual design are top notch. Sometimes inputs are a bit delayed like you're chaining attacks and using items I had to press the keys multiple times (yes my controllers are fine). The parry is kind of hard to time and takes time to get used to. All boss fights are traumatic memorable.

Overall, I'd recommend this to hardcore soulslike player, but if you're starting out you will have a rough experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that player characters lack poise and hyperarmor, while standard enemies and bosses possess infinite poise during their attack strings.

citations.review_text:
I finished the game, but I do not recommend it. There is merit to this game, and it improves greatly on a lot of the old souls formula, but it has some flaws which make me not want to play it again. I beat the game with a motivity/capacity build, basically a STR/Carry capacity build. I enjoyed it a lot in the beginning but as the game went on, it became apparent that if there was something I didn't like, I would be running into it a lot.

- You as the player have effectively no poise/hyperarmor except for a handful of attacks while even the lowliest enemy has poise/hyperarmor on a significant number of attacks. This combination makes it so you don't feel like you're growing stronger with levels, and it makes level exploration a bit of an unfun chore

- Every single enemy has a fast attack combo in which they have infinite poise. If you try to trade, you will get slapped down by literally every enemy

- The game's core mechanic revolves around parrying and attacking until the enemy's stance breaks, after which you can do a heavy attack which leaves the enemy open for a finisher. Partway through, the game will punish you for this by giving bosses an attack triggered by your heavy attack. The boss gets to attack you because you're beating it too hard.

- Many bosses flail wildly, with noodly unclear appendages, making it difficult to successfully predict the parry window

- Many boss recovery animations look like another attack. It makes you hesitate, which means you lose your attack window

- Most bosses have full hyperarmor attacks which consist of a long windup, followed by a pause, followed by a near instant attack. The game really doesn't want you to reaction parry. It wants you to effectively learn by failing.

- Almost every mandatory boss has 2 phases

- You have very little forward momentum as you attack, but bosses will slide across the arena to reach you. Your weapon is shorter than it seems.

- After a certain point in the game, all bosses…

I have some kinda big issues with it, but it's a wonderful soulslike.
Whoever designed how poise works deserves a demotion.
The world building is the best part of this game, there are some really bad bossfights (they arent hard, just frustrating and generally not fun, this game is easy asf) so be prepared for that, but the atmosphere mostly makes up for it.

If they start using AI for the next project, I will change this to a negative review and boycott.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features multiple difficulty settings, allowing players to adjust the challenge if they find the default experience too difficult.

citations.review_text: Even though it's not from Fromsoftware but this game is still on a different level. I've completed Sekiro, Elden Ring, Black Myth Wukong, and other soulslike game. But this one gives you mix of all of them. Here parry isn't necessary but dogding won't gonna always help you either. The game teaches you mechanic throughout the game without bombarding with unreadable popups. Every level have its own set of enemies that teaches you to beat the final boss of that level. The design and art of this game is mind blowing too. Overall if you're a new to soulslike game, you can definitely try this game since now they've also added difficulty bar. But that's something I didn't like because it breaks the purpose of the game. But people playing with Legendary Stalker difficulty will know how beautifully challenging this game is.

Actual Fromsoft level Souls Like. 
Even more, this game does bunch of things better than Fromsoftware: 
- Boss Rematches
- Neither NPC questlines, nor story is as esoteric as Fromsoft
- More diverse options of RPG (Levels, P Organ, Legion Arm etc.) and their respective respec
- Build variety due to Weapon Handle/Blade system
- Personally I like parry here more, than in Sekiro (In Sekiro parry window is earlier than in Lies of P)
- Difficulty Settings - I am glad they tuned the game for hardest difficulty and then added some easier difficulties, so that more people can enjoy.

Also, don't be scared after seeing Unreal Engine. Game's optimization is superb. Also game is beautiful af.

My only complaints:
- Game is too linear, which I don't love
- Last bosses of base game and DLC involve bosses with some of the most disgusting/♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moves.

Overall, great game!

This was my first true Soulslike so I was a little intimidated since I've had no experience with the genre before, but after getting used to the controls I found everything intuitive and enjoyable. Even though the game was incredibly challenging the whole way through, there were plenty of ways to make things easier, from using summons during boss fights, having plenty of weapon options and other charms that switches up playstyle, and even dropping difficulty levels if necessary. I played on highest difficulty through my first playthrough and it never felt unfair.
The parry mechanic is an added challenge, but it becomes incredibly satisfying when you get the hang of it. The runback from the bosses weren't too terrible either. The level designs are fairly streamlined, even though there's no map systems at all, so I never really found myself lost or turned around too badly.
However, I do have a major gripe to share: it is insanely easy to get the bad ending to this game, and there is a hard save mechanic, so if you make a choice you regret you have to play through THE ENTIRITY OF THE GAME OVER AGAIN if you want to get a different ending. The Overture DLC (which I have not purchased yet) can also only be activated over halfway through the game, so I'll probably have to play through a third time if I choose to get the DLC, which is a major downside for me.
Overall, though, this is a beautiful and well-crafted game, and for anybody wondering whether this game is a gentle entry into the SoulsBorne genre, from my experience I can say it was a decent introduction!

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the dodge roll mechanic feels weak or ineffective during combat encounters.

citations.review_text: I am only recommending this because if you look at the game objectively from the souls like perspective it is a great souls-like. Personally, I did not like the game. It took me around 15 hours to even start enjoying it. I uninstalled an reinstalled numerous times because I got bored. I don't like the aesthetic. I had to download the blood borne armor mod because I hated looking at the stupid twink main character. The weapons are boring. The fable arts system is ok but it takes too long to charge for your first playthrough. The characters are not interesting. The combat is ok but the dodge roll is terrible and the parry is not as good as Sekiro. Everything about this game was boring. I will never play it again.

I like the story and atmosphere, but what this game is at the end of the day is a souls-like with a bad dodge and an even worse parry, the two fundamental combat elements of the genre.  A lot of the game is very frustrating because you are fighting with the exceptionally bad parry timing.  You have to block really early in the animation so if the attack has already started, you are too late.  It is poor design and extremely frustrating in what could be a great game otherwise.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is well-optimized and runs smoothly on hardware, though one notes encountering a memory leak leading to frame rate drops after extended play.

citations.review_text:
Great game. Great story, graphics and combat gameplay. Weapon customization creates a lot of fun weapons and the boss weapons are also very fun to play with. 
Worth the buy. DLC that you have buy separately was the cherry on top. 

One more thing worth mentioning, this game is extremely very optimized. This gives me by far the best FPS on my old hardware as well as my new hardware.

The bosses, mechanics, sound design and level design are perfect in my opinion, the only issue I have is there's a memory leak because of my card so my fps drops to 30 after playing for about an hour or so.

This is by far my favourite souls like game.

This is one of the best games I've ever played. It's got great gameplay, story, sound, and world. Excellent graphics and really well optimized.

I've beat it multiple times, the DLC is really good, too.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the world design is linear with limited branching paths and minimal exploration compared to traditional open-world games.

citations.review_text:
Lies of P is an amazing game. This is the single best souls like that isn't made by fromsoft, and even then it might be able to topple their games.

This work shows that they understand what makes souls games good, and they took everything they needed out of it for Lies of P. The atmosphere is perfect for the game. Exploring is fun although fans of souls games will find it much more linear in design, with only a few branching paths that reconverge shortly after. Within that linearity are plenty of secrets and hidden items to find, so I didn't mind at all, I even prefer it over DS3, which is also my closest comparison for Lies of P's level design. The story giving you a lot more character interactions, emotional beats, and lore to chew on. I was able to care about and feel for characters in this game much more than any other soulslike i've played. I still think about the implications of Ergo at least every other month, it expands on souls and I, Robot in a very interesting way. The music and especially the records are beautiful pieces.

Alright, gameplay. It's really really good. Closest comparisons I can make are bloodborne and sekiro. You want to be perfect guarding as many hits as you can, dodging is a little safer with less reward, and dodging twice is a little dangerous but has a big safety window. Some criticize the lack of a visible stagger bar, but I never had an issue with it. It's more of a nice surprise that you get for doing exceptionally well, and you can choose to play safe and not take advantage of it, or you can play risky for massive payoff when you see it. Your healing potions are better here than any other souls game, this is by far my favorite. You get a certain amount of them when you leave the checkpoint, then when you run out, you can build one back up by dealing damage. This makes it so that when you're low on health you still want to play aggressively. This really encourages learning and mastering the boss movesets to beat them. The challenge…

Not enough options to modify controller buttons and cannot set fast responding direct hotkeys like on a keyboard. Therefor this game does not suit game consoles. With fast fingers and the in-game battle animations where you can't do anything during those animation, this game becomes slow and frustrating. Further more it's a linear game, your path is set all the way so don't expect creative solutions to progress in all situations. It's basically Donkey Kong or Prince of Persia i.e. upgraded in 3D.
Its a good game but sadly quite linear so if you like the exploration this game sadly misses that. Other than that the game is pretty sweet and has a banging ost

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as heavily reliant on perfect guarding and parrying mechanics, noting that dodging is a viable alternative though with different risk and reward balances.

You get a certain amount of them when you leave the checkpoint, then when you run out, you can build one back up by dealing damage. This makes it so that when you're low on health you still want to play aggressively. This really encourages learning and mastering the boss movesets to beat them. The challenge…

Lies of P is a bone fide souls game, not a souls-like. It wasn't made by from soft but it stands shoulder to shoulder with from soft's greats. It was my game of the year in 2023, and though it got its flowers as a good game I think that still sells it short. Its a GREAT game, or more accurately a masterpiece. It merges the gameplay styles of Souls (stamina, dodge/block based combat and RPG elements) seamlessly with the Sekiro parry system, which to date still hasnt been done effectively by from soft themselves. Round 8 did their homework, and while some people call Lies of P plagiaristic I see a love letter to from soft, and not without its own innovations and identity. The game is gorgeous with a magical soundtrack. It has arguably the best boss roster in any souls game, rivaled only by Dark Souls 3. Its combat and aesthetic level design are top notch for the sub genre. Its got a great and more direct story that still tackles the concept of humanity that made the souls games stories so moving. This game is the full package and is still underrated in my humble opinion.

After 100+ hours and counting, and 100% achievement, all I can say is P-organ does wonder to a person. Yes you heard it correctly: P-ORGAN.

Jokes aside, game is fantastic, gameplay is souls-like (except if you decide to roll instead of perfect guard - i.e. parrying, it will make your gameplay experience not complete, but again you should play the game however you like and enjoy). 

ALSO for storyline progression, you should play the DLC after you have finished chapter 10 in the base game, or 9 if you feel like you are up to the level scaling in DLC. Other than that, enjoy the ride, and you should do a first blind playthrough (no guides, no backseating, no external sources help) before you aim for achievement completion for a wonderful gameplay and story experience
